# Vibe Coding Starter

> A Korean-first guide and Next.js boilerplate for complete beginners on Windows and macOS. It teaches a four-stage vibe-coding session: environment setup, ideation, Goal planning, and review.

Repository: https://github.com/coolseaweed/vibecoding
Website: https://vibecoding-pied-ten.vercel.app
Language: Korean, with English tool and command names preserved
Package manager: Bun only
Audience: complete beginners who may not have GitHub, Vercel, or Supabase accounts

## Start here

- docs/checklist/README.md — environment review for Git, GitHub, Bun, Vercel, Supabase, MCP, and security
- docs/workflow/README.md — the canonical four-stage workflow, one-shot prompt, and completion criteria
- docs/git/README.md — account creation, Windows and macOS installation, fork, clone, commit, and troubleshooting
- docs/mcp/README.md — ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Codex, and Claude Code setup for Vercel and Supabase MCP
- docs/deploy/README.md — account creation, fork-based Vercel deployment, development Supabase setup, verification, and rollback
- docs/doctor/README.md — repository-only checklist for Git, Vercel, Supabase, and MCP connections

The public website is a single page at `/`. Markdown files under `docs` remain repository-only reference material.

## Required workflow

1. Environment setup: verify the OS, accounts, Git identity, GitHub authentication, Bun, repository status, local run, checks, and MCP scope.
2. Ideation: define the user and problem, compare at least three approaches, choose the smallest valuable direction, and state non-goals.
3. Planning (Goal): write a user outcome, scope, non-goals, constraints, and binary success criteria. Pair every task with verification.
4. Review: inspect the diff, run deterministic checks, manually test desktop and mobile, review security and accessibility, and issue a pass / needs changes / blocked verdict.

If review fails, return to the earliest stage that caused the failure and repeat the loop.

## Repository commands

```bash
bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun dev
bun run lint
bun run typecheck
bun run build
bun run check
```

Do not use npm, yarn, or pnpm. Do not add environment variables until the feature requiring them is approved. Never commit secrets or `.env` files.

## MCP configuration

- Codex repository config: `.codex/config.toml`
- Claude Code repository config: `.mcp.json`
- Vercel project MCP: `https://mcp.vercel.com/coolseaweeds-projects/vibecoding`
- Supabase safe default: docs-only, read-only remote MCP until a real development project ref exists

Repository-scoped config does not automatically restrict service permissions to one cloud project. ChatGPT and Claude Desktop do not read these repository files. Read `docs/mcp/README.md` before authentication. Prefer OAuth and manual confirmation. Scope Supabase to a development `project_ref`, `read_only=true`, and minimum features before enabling database tools.

## One-shot agent contract

Before editing, read `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `docs/workflow/README.md`, and the relevant guide. Inspect git status and existing configuration. State assumptions when information is missing.

If no Goal with user, problem, scope, and acceptance criteria is supplied, do not invent or implement a feature. Return the missing-input template from `docs/workflow/README.md` and wait.

Use the minimum change that satisfies the Goal. Preserve unrelated work. Do not create secrets, paid resources, production deployments, or destructive database changes without explicit authorization.

Completion requires:

- the requested user flow works;
- `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, and `bun run build` pass;
- relevant browser checks pass on desktop and mobile;
- no secrets or unintended files are staged;
- the final report names evidence, deployment URL when requested, and any remaining limitation.

## Evaluation criteria

Judge every result on four criteria:

1. A complete beginner can create GitHub, Vercel, and Supabase accounts and finish setup without unstated prerequisites.
2. Instructions use short steps, define unfamiliar terms, and avoid unnecessary choices.
3. The one-shot request produces the stated Goal accurately with explicit verification evidence.
4. A reader with no prior coding knowledge can understand the repository documents without outside explanation.
